question: Should Signal setup save native configurations after daemon/RPC reachability while requiring pre-save linked-account and receive validation for container servers?
rationale: Native SSE can remain idle before producing headers, so it cannot use the same bounded readiness check as the container WebSocket path; the operator-facing meaning of “ready” requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept transport-specific readiness
options.body: Keep the implementation and document that native receive becomes established when the monitor connects, while container account and receive readiness are validated before saving.

options.title: Narrow the readiness claim
options.body: Describe native setup as daemon reachability rather than receive readiness until the monitor successfully connects.

options.title: Require stronger native validation
options.body: Delay the feature until a bounded native account or receive validation mechanism can be implemented and proven.

recommendation.title: Accept transport-specific readiness
recommendation.body: Keep the implementation and document that native receive becomes established when the monitor connects, while container account and receive readiness are validated before saving.

likelyOwner.reason: Jesse has several previously merged Signal runtime features and owns the proposed setup behavior most directly.
